narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 72.5% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. In practical terms, the school treated that as a high risk that you would not meet its bar-passage expectations, so it rejected your admission application despite other strengths.

The strongest reason was your third-year class standing: you were in the lowest decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile. This was the single most influential factor and pushed the prediction toward failure. Your first-year standing was also in the lowest decile, again far below the accepted-student average near the sixth decile, and it was the second most important factor pushing toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.20 was the third most important factor; relative to the other concerns, it was a slight protective factor that pushed toward passing, even though it is just below the accepted average of about 3.23.

To improve your chances, focus on raising your academic standing in advanced law coursework if possible, consult the admissions office about whether additional courses or a delayed application could strengthen your record, and consider retaking the LSAT to show stronger exam readiness. Ask for specific guidance on what evidence would offset the third-year rank concern.
